document_title: More Than Three Alaskas of Power, Planned for Prudhoe Bay
post_copy:
3,000 megawatts. Phase one of a gas plant planned near Prudhoe Bay for AI data centers nearly equals all 152 power plants in Alaska.

The full plan is 10,000 megawatts, more than three times that fleet. Behind it is North Slope Power, the North Slope Borough's venture with Twenty First Century Utilities.

The Alaska Current's reporting adds up to $6.2 million of public money so far. It quotes the $5 million resolution saying the Borough would "initially" keep majority ownership. The financial structure is not public. It should be, before a plant this size goes up.

What EIA measures is drawn sharp, all 152 plants mapped to scale. The reported money sits in fog. The terms are a closed pipe blind.

Before the next public dollar goes in, what is the strongest case for keeping the terms private?

#NorthSlopeBorough #PrudhoeBay #DataCenterPower

slides.headline: More than three Alaskas of power, planned for Prudhoe Bay.
Each lit bore is 100 MW.
slides.body: Phase one is about the size of every power plant in Alaska combined. The full plan is more than three times it.
labels: INSTALLED CAPACITY, EIA. PLAN FIGURES AS REPORTED.

slides.kicker: EVERY POWER PLANT IN ALASKA, TO SCALE
slides.headline: A borough's plant, for AI data centers.
slides.body: The North Slope Borough and Twenty First Century Utilities (TFC) are developing North Slope Power to feed colocated AI data centers. The borough's own utility runs seven village plants, 21.4 MW in all.
labels: DISC AREA IS INSTALLED MW. 152 PLANTS, EIA.

slides.headline: The gas is already here.
slides.body: Two outlets, two areas, two counts. Gas is already Alaska's main fuel for electricity, per EIA. In March the borough's mayor and TFC took the plan to CERAWeek in Texas.

slides.headline: TFC's proposal listed climate change among 10 North Slope challenges. Where it said how it would tackle each one, climate change got "N/A."
labels: AS THE ALASKA CURRENT DESCRIBES THE PROPOSAL

slides.headline: $6.2 million in.
slides.body: A $1.2 million no-bid feasibility contract in November 2025. Another $5 million of public funds in March. Both as reported by the Alaska Current.

slides.headline: The terms aren't public.
slides.body: That is the resolution behind the $5 million, as the Alaska Current quotes it. It says the Borough would "initially" keep that majority. The financial structure is not public.
labels: "an investor-owned utility (IOU) with Borough majority ownership"

The Alaska Current reports that the North Slope Borough election is Tuesday, October 6th. Keep the post and every reply about the plant, the public money and the terms, not the vote or the mayor, so it isn't read as election commentary. editor_notes_for_email: Every fact about the borough comes from secondary reporting. The $1.2 million and $5 million, the resolution's wording, the pipeline and the proposal's N/A come from the Alaska Current on October 3rd; the 3 GW to 10 GW plan, the gas count and CERAWeek also from Dermot Cole on May 12th. The primary sources are EIA (152 plants, 3,106.5 MW installed nameplate, the borough's seven village plants at 21.4 MW, gas as the state's main fuel). Resolutions 13-2026 and 84-2025 couldn't be read directly (the borough's SharePoint viewer returned no text; downloads failed 401 and 404), so both are quoted as the Current reported them and the first comment says so. Phase one is compared on installed nameplate capacity (97 percent of Alaska; the full plan 3.22 times). EIA's 2,853 MW net summer figure would give 1.05 and 3.5 and is kept off the slides. Campaign contributions to the mayor, Tuesday's vote and the earlier recall efforts were left out on purpose: single-outlet sourcing days before an election.
